resume_text:
Marcus Feld
Staff-level Backend Engineer | Seattle, WA | marcus.feld@example.com | (206) 555-0174
linkedin.com/in/marcusfeld

SUMMARY
Eight years on distributed backend systems, the last four at the scale where the interesting
problems are coordination and failure rather than throughput. Java and Kotlin on the JVM,
with the operational half of the job included rather than handed off.

EXPERIENCE

Pellar Freight - Senior Software Engineer
Seattle, WA | Jan 2021 - Present
- Technical lead for the shipment orchestration platform: 9 services, 22 engineers across
  three teams consuming it, 1.4 million shipment state transitions a day.
- Designed and led the migration of order state management from synchronous service calls
  to an event-driven model on Kafka, which removed the cascading timeout failures that had
  caused 6 of the previous year's 11 Sev-1 incidents.
- Introduced the transactional outbox pattern across 7 services, eliminating the dual-write
  inconsistencies that had been generating roughly 200 manual data corrections a month.
- Cut p99 shipment creation latency from 3.1s to 780ms by removing three synchronous
  dependencies from the critical path and moving them behind events.
- Led the sharding of the shipments Postgres database at 2.4 billion rows, executed live
  over eleven weeks with no customer-visible downtime.
- Wrote the service template and paved road that all new JVM services are generated from:
  observability, health checks, graceful shutdown and CI included by default.
- Ran the on-call rotation redesign across three teams; pages per engineer per week fell
  from 11 to 3 while the Sev-1 count also fell.
- Interviewed roughly 120 candidates and rewrote the backend system design rubric after a
  calibration exercise showed two interviewers disagreeing on a third of signals.

Harlow Systems - Software Engineer
Portland, OR | Aug 2017 - Dec 2020
- Built and owned the billing calculation service in Java and Spring Boot, processing
  around $40 million a month in invoices.
- Rewrote the tax rule engine, reducing a class of rounding defects that had produced 30 to
  40 support escalations a quarter to effectively zero.
- Added contract testing with Pact between billing and four consuming services, which
  caught 17 breaking changes before release in the first year.
- Reduced the build and test cycle from 26 minutes to 7 by parallelising the integration
  suite and using Testcontainers instead of a shared staging database.

EDUCATION
M.S. Computer Science, Oregon State University, 2015 - 2017
B.S. Computer Science, Oregon State University, 2011 - 2015

SKILLS
Languages: Java (17, 21), Kotlin, SQL, Python
Frameworks: Spring Boot, Spring Cloud, Micronaut, JUnit 5, Testcontainers, Pact
Data: PostgreSQL, Kafka, Redis, Elasticsearch, DynamoDB
Distributed systems: event-driven architecture, sagas, transactional outbox, idempotency,
CQRS, sharding, consistency tradeoffs
Infrastructure: AWS, Kubernetes, Terraform, Docker, GitHub Actions
Observability: OpenTelemetry, Datadog, Prometheus, Grafana
jd_text:
Staff Software Engineer, Backend Platform
Seattle, WA (Hybrid, 2 days) or Remote US | $215,000 - $265,000 + equity

We are a marketplace processing around 3 million orders a day. Backend platform is the
group that owns the shared services everything else is built on: order state, identity,
messaging infrastructure and the deployment path for JVM services.

We are hiring a staff engineer. The distinction we draw is that a senior engineer owns a
system and a staff engineer owns a problem that spans systems and teams, including the
parts of it that are organisational. If you want to be handed a well-defined service and
left alone, this is the wrong posting and we mean that kindly.

You will
- Set technical direction for order and fulfilment state management across roughly 40
  services and six teams
- Lead migrations that take quarters rather than sprints, including the part where you keep
  six teams aligned on a plan none of them proposed
- Design event-driven systems on Kafka, and be the person who is rigorous about delivery
  semantics, ordering guarantees and idempotency when others are not
- Own database scaling decisions: partitioning, sharding, read replica strategy, and the
  migrations to get there without downtime
- Raise the operational bar. SLOs, on-call load, incident review quality
- Write design documents that change what other teams do, and review theirs

Requirements
- 8+ years of backend engineering, including several at senior level with scope beyond your
  own team
- Deep JVM experience: Java or Kotlin, Spring Boot or equivalent, and a working
  understanding of what the runtime is doing
- Distributed systems in production: you have designed for partial failure, not just read
  about it. Sagas, outbox, exactly-once-in-effect semantics, backpressure
- Kafka or a comparable log-based broker, at a scale where topic and partition design
  mattered
- PostgreSQL at large scale, including at least one migration you would describe as
  frightening
- Demonstrated technical leadership: a migration you led across teams, a standard you set
  that outlived your involvement
- Strong written communication. Our design review culture is written, not presented

Nice to have
- Kubernetes and Terraform at ownership level
- OpenTelemetry and distributed tracing rollouts
- Marketplace, logistics or fulfilment domain
- Having built an internal platform or paved road that other engineers chose to use
- Interview process design or engineering hiring calibration

Process: recruiter call, a systems design round on one of our real past problems, a code
and collaboration round, a leadership round with two staff engineers, and a conversation
with the VP. We share the design prompt in advance because we are not testing your ability
to be surprised.
